decisions.what_it_tests: What information is visible at each protocol layer (a layer-4 device cannot see the user).
decisions.why_this_topic: The deciding idea is which header fields exist up to the transport layer: IPs, ports and protocol are visible, but the identity of a user on a multi-user host is not. That is layering knowledge, the closest 2027 topic since firewalls themselves are not in the syllabus.

alternatives_considered.why_not: No application-protocol behaviour is needed; HTTP is blockable by port 80 at layer 4.

decisions.solution_sketch: A: block port 80 by time - possible. B: ICMP is a protocol field - possible. C: stateful IP filtering - possible. D: user identity is not in any L2-L4 header - impossible.
decisions.note: Firewalls are not in the 2027 syllabus; CN.LAYER is the nearest fit.

decisions.what_it_tests: Conditional probability with a reduced sample space.
decisions.why_this_topic: Given at least one head, the sample space shrinks to {HH, HT, TH}; only HH qualifies. This is textbook conditional probability (Probability: conditional probability and Bayes theorem in the EM syllabus).

alternatives_considered.why_not: Counting the outcomes is trivial; the idea tested is conditioning.

decisions.solution_sketch: P(HH | at least one H) = (1/4)/(3/4) = 1/3.
decisions.note: Clear.

decisions.what_it_tests: Which application protocol carries each email activity (SMTP push, POP pull, HTTP webmail).
decisions.why_this_topic: Pure application-layer protocol roles: sending mail uses SMTP, downloading uses POP, browser webmail uses HTTP. The 2027 application-layer topic (DNS, SMTP, HTTP, FTP, email) covers it.

alternatives_considered.why_not: No layering reasoning; only protocol-to-task mapping.

decisions.solution_sketch: m1 SMTP, m2 POP, m3 HTTP -> option C.
decisions.note: Clear.

decisions.what_it_tests: Break-even LOC between two languages from development + maintenance cost.
decisions.why_this_topic: A software project cost estimation problem; software engineering was removed from the GATE CS syllabus, so it belongs in the historical LEGACY.SE section under estimation.

alternatives_considered.why_not: The arithmetic is simple, but the setting and intent are SE cost estimation.

decisions.note: Topic right, but the last sentence of the stem is garbled by OCR ('Tot t o t e a ... or which') - fix the text from the PDF.

decisions.what_it_tests: A mode switch is cheaper than a process context switch.
decisions.why_this_topic: The answer depends on knowing what a process switch saves and restores (registers, memory map, TLB) compared with a mode switch. That is process-model knowledge (Processes, threads and context switching).

alternatives_considered.why_not: No scheduling policy is involved; only the cost of the switch.

decisions.solution_sketch: Process switch includes a mode switch plus saving/restoring state, so t1 < t2.
decisions.note: OCR wrote 't' for t1 in places; meaning is clear.

decisions.what_it_tests: Basic COCOMO effort formula E = a * KLOC^b.
decisions.why_this_topic: COCOMO is a software effort-estimation model from the old SE syllabus; nothing in the 2027 syllabus covers it.
decisions.note: Clear.

decisions.what_it_tests: Determinism changes the power of pushdown automata but not of finite automata or Turing machines.
decisions.why_this_topic: The only pair that differs is DPDA vs NPDA, so the deciding fact is about pushdown automata (context-free grammars and push-down automata). The other options test known equivalences as distractors.

alternatives_considered.why_not: DFA = NFA is only a distractor.
TM equivalences are distractors, not the answer.

decisions.solution_sketch: DFA = NFA, deterministic TM = non-deterministic TM, single-tape = multi-tape TM; DPDA is strictly weaker than NPDA.
decisions.note: Spans three machine models; PDA is the deciding one.

decisions.what_it_tests: What plain HTML can do without scripting (meta refresh/redirect yes, show client time no).
decisions.why_this_topic: HTML / web technologies were in the old syllabus but are not in GATE CS 2027, and LEGACY only holds software engineering. CN.APP (HTTP) is the nearest home, but it is a weak fit.

alternatives_considered.why_not: Web technology is not software engineering.

decisions.solution_sketch: Embedding objects (iframe/img) and meta refresh/redirect are pure HTML; showing the client's clock needs a script.
decisions.note: Out of the 2027 syllabus (web technologies). Consider a LEGACY.WEB topic - part of the out-of-syllabus decision.

decisions.what_it_tests: An SRS states what, not how - algorithms do not belong in it.
decisions.why_this_topic: Requirements specification is a classic old-syllabus software engineering topic (requirements).
decisions.solution_sketch: Functional, non-functional requirements and goals belong; implementation algorithms do not.
decisions.note: Clear.

decisions.what_it_tests: Interrupt priority: critical hardware faults come first.
decisions.why_this_topic: The question is about choosing priorities among interrupt sources, which is the interrupt part of 'I/O interface (interrupt and DMA mode)'.

alternatives_considered.why_not: No process scheduling; hardware interrupt priority.

decisions.solution_sketch: Overheating can damage the CPU and must be handled first -> CPU temperature sensor.
decisions.note: Label was flagged earlier; topic is right.

decisions.what_it_tests: Superkey, candidate key and primary key definitions applied to attributes.
decisions.why_this_topic: Every option asks whether an attribute set is a candidate key, primary key or superkey; no functional dependencies or normal forms are used. Keys sit under the relational model in our taxonomy.

alternatives_considered.why_not: Integrity constraints/normal forms would need FDs or normalisation, which are absent.

decisions.solution_sketch: Joint accounts mean two students can share BankAccount_Num, so it is not unique and not a candidate key -> A is the incorrect statement.
decisions.note: Option D lost a symbol in extraction ('S UUID' should be S union UID).

decisions.what_it_tests: Minimising a product-of-sums expression to SOP.
decisions.why_this_topic: Simplifying a Boolean expression is Boolean algebra and minimization. Topic is right.
decisions.solution_sketch: Cannot be solved reliably: the complement bars on P, Q, R were lost and the four options are merged into the stem.
decisions.note: Stored as NAT but it is an MCQ with options (A)-(D) inside the stem; complement bars lost. Fix type, text and options from the PDF.

decisions.what_it_tests: What state is per-thread versus shared per-process.
decisions.why_this_topic: Threads share the address space, so the OS keeps no separate virtual-memory state per thread. This is the threads part of 'Processes, threads, inter-process communication'.

alternatives_considered.why_not: Virtual memory is only the object being shared; the question is about the thread model.

decisions.solution_sketch: Per thread: registers, stack, scheduling info. Shared: address space. So C is true; A, B, D are false.
decisions.note: Clear.

decisions.what_it_tests: Planarity of K4 and the 3-cube Q3.
decisions.why_this_topic: Planarity is graph theory, which sits in Discrete Mathematics (graphs: connectivity, matching, colouring) in EM, not in the algorithms or data structures sections.
decisions.solution_sketch: K4 can be drawn without crossings; Q3 is also planar (a square inside a square). Both planar -> B.
decisions.note: The graph figures are not in the text (image only); option C says K3 where the paper has K4.

decisions.what_it_tests: Variance E[X^2] - (E[X])^2 is never negative.
decisions.why_this_topic: The quantity is the variance of a random variable; knowing it is non-negative is random-variable basics (mean, variance).
decisions.solution_sketch: R = Var(X) >= 0, with equality for a constant -> C.
decisions.note: Stored as NAT but it is an MCQ - options (A)-(D) are inside the stem. Topic right.

decisions.what_it_tests: Tokens are regular, so a lexer needs exactly finite automata.
decisions.why_this_topic: The question is framed around lexical analysis of a programming language, which the 2027 syllabus lists under Compiler Design (lexical analysis). The automata knowledge it needs is a secondary topic.

alternatives_considered.why_not: Plausible, since the answer is 'finite automata', but the question asks about a compiler phase, not about a language.

decisions.solution_sketch: Token patterns are regular expressions -> finite state automata are necessary and sufficient.
decisions.note: Genuine CD/TOC boundary case - your call; I lean CD.LEX.

decisions.what_it_tests: Recognising base + displacement addressing in LW R1, 20(R2).
decisions.why_this_topic: Pure addressing-mode identification (machine instructions and addressing modes).
decisions.solution_sketch: Effective address = constant + register contents -> base (indexed/displacement) addressing -> D.
decisions.note: Clear.

decisions.what_it_tests: Pointer arithmetic using character values as offsets.
decisions.why_this_topic: Tracing a C expression with char arithmetic and pointer offsets is 'Programming in C'. No existing concept fits (PDS.C.SCOPE is about scope), so concepts are left empty.

alternatives_considered.why_not: The array is only the container; the skill is pointer arithmetic.

decisions.solution_sketch: p[3]='E', p[1]='A', difference 4 -> printf from c+4 -> "2011".
decisions.note: A 'pointers' concept under PDS.C would help many questions like this.

decisions.what_it_tests: Recognising a recurrence over subproblems as dynamic programming.
decisions.why_this_topic: L_i is computed from L_(i+1), a stored subproblem result, which is the dynamic programming paradigm (algorithm design techniques).

alternatives_considered.why_not: Complexity appears in options but the correct choice is about the paradigm.

decisions.solution_sketch: One backward pass with a recurrence -> linear DP; no branch and bound or divide and conquer -> A.
decisions.note: Topic right; the label's extra concept ALGO.DESIGN.DAC is wrong - only DP applies.

decisions.what_it_tests: Classifying 0^p1^q, 0^p1^p and 0^p1^p0^p as regular / context-free / neither.
decisions.why_this_topic: The task is deciding which language class each language belongs to, which is 'Regular and context-free languages, pumping lemma'. L3 not being context-free is the deciding fact.

alternatives_considered.why_not: No grammar or PDA has to be built; only class membership.

decisions.solution_sketch: L1 regular, L2 CFL not regular, L3 not CFL. So 'all three are context free' is NOT true -> C.
decisions.note: Superscripts were lost in extraction ('0P19' = 0^p 1^q) - fix the text from the PDF.
